rics.meaning: Export prices, all commodities — BLS monthly.
rics.how_to_use: Reflects US producer pricing power abroad. Combined with import prices gives terms-of-trade signal.

rics.meaning: Export prices, nonagricultural commodities — strips out volatile food/farm exports.
rics.how_to_use: Better signal of manufactured-goods pricing. Cleaner trend than the headline.
Released ~mid-month. Early read on global demand for US goods. Exports prices YoY ≈ goods exports inflation.
Direct inflation pass-through to consumer prices. Crude oil moves are the dominant driver historically.

rics.description: Import Prices, All imports excluding petroleum
rics.meaning: Import prices excluding petroleum — strips out the biggest source of volatility.
rics.how_to_use: Cleaner core-import-inflation measure. Pair with USD trade-weighted to identify FX vs underlying global price drivers.
Released alongside export prices. Direct CPI input — feeds goods inflation 1-2 months out.

rics.description: Export Prices, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.how_to_use: Quarterly aggregation of monthly. Use for cross-country comparison via OECD framework.

rics.description: Export Prices, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Export Prices, year-over-year change (standardized) — pace of US export-price change. Reflects US producer pricing power abroad and currency effects.
rics.how_to_use: Track alongside import prices for terms-of-trade signal. When export prices rise faster than import prices, terms of trade improve (US gets more imports per export). Currency-driven mostly: dollar strength compresses export prices in dollar terms.

rics.meaning: Export Prices, standardized index — companion to aUSEXPP at standardized framing for international comparison.
rics.how_to_use: Use for cross-country export-price comparisons. Domestic analysts use aUSEXPP. Standardization aligns with IMF/OECD cross-border statistics conventions.

rics.description: Import Prices, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.how_to_use: Quarterly version. Pairs with export QoQ for terms-of-trade.

rics.description: Import Prices, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.how_to_use: Pass-through to CPI is highest in goods categories; services CPI mostly domestic.

rics.meaning: Import Prices, standardized index — companion to aUSIMPP at standardized framing.
rics.how_to_use: Direct CPI input — feeds goods inflation. Crude oil moves are biggest single driver. Watch alongside dollar (DXY) for currency-pass-through to consumer prices.

rics.description: Terms of Trade, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Terms-of-trade QoQ change — export prices / import prices.
rics.how_to_use: Improving (rising) ToT = country gets more imports per unit of exports = real income transfer in.

rics.description: Terms of Trade, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.how_to_use: Big oil price moves swing ToT for net importers/exporters. US flipped to net energy exporter, so oil shocks now help ToT.

rics.meaning: Terms of Trade, standardized — ratio of export prices to import prices. Measures how much imports a country gets per unit of export.
rics.how_to_use: Improving terms of trade = country gets more for less = real-income gain. US terms of trade improved post-shale (energy import collapse) but worsened during commodity-import surges. Watch for major shifts as macro-cycle signals.
Long history version. Useful for showing decade-scale ToT trends.

rics.meaning: Advance Goods Trade Balance — preliminary monthly goods-only deficit.
rics.how_to_use: Released ~3 days before the full BEA trade report. Goods-only (services excluded). Big surprises move the dollar at release.
